subject: social-studies
title: Neighbourhood Change: One Site, Stage by Stage Exit Ticket

questions.prompt: A student says A neighbourhood changes all at once, because the new flats, shops and MRT station all appear in a single step. What is the best correction?

choices.text: The student is right - the photographs prove it changed overnight

A neighbourhood changes stage by stage: transport links arrive first as the MRT station and bus stop open, housing blocks then rise plot by plot, and only as families move in do the shops, market and school open - the population grows at every stage, not in one jump.
The neighbourhood changed all at once, but more slowly
The MRT station appeared last, after the shops and school opened

questions.misconception: A neighbourhood changes all at once, because the new flats, shops and MRT station all appear in a single step.
questions.feedback: If you agreed with the student, that is the trap: A neighbourhood changes all at once, because the new flats, shops and MRT station all appear in a single step. Reteach point: A neighbourhood changes stage by stage: transport links arrive first as the MRT station and bus stop open, housing blocks then rise plot by plot, and only as families move in do the shops, market and school open - the population grows at every stage, not in one jump.

questions.prompt: In one sentence, explain why transport arrives before the housing blocks.
questions.answer: Transport arrives first so the site is easy to reach: the MRT station and bus stop open before the blocks rise, so the families who move in can travel to and from the neighbourhood.
questions.feedback: A strong answer names the order - station and bus stop first, blocks after - and the reason: people need a way to reach the new homes.

questions.prompt: In the final stage, the corrected replay shows the neighbourhood changing:

choices.text: All at once, in a single step
Stage by stage - transport first, blocks plot by plot, then shops, market and school as families arrive
Backwards, from the school to the open ground
Only in photographs, never on the site itself

questions.feedback: Scene 4 flashes everything in together as the wrong turn, then replays the true sequence stage by stage with the population bar climbing at every stage.

questions.prompt: In one sentence, state the final stage of the change and the stages that came before it.
questions.answer: The final stage is the corrected replay - change happens stage by stage - and it came after low-rise houses and open ground, transport arriving first, and housing blocks rising plot by plot as shops, a market and a school opened for the families moving in.
questions.feedback: A strong answer gives the whole order - houses and open ground, transport first, blocks plot by plot, shops, market and school - with no stage skipped.
